records.rationale: This is a broad MAS tutorial with no empirical software-development evaluation or substantive mechanism evidence.
The study evaluates single-LLM software configuration and hallucination risks, providing indirect benchmark context but no multi-agent evidence.
This review catalogs LLM vulnerability detection and repair methods and limitations that can support security assurance for agent-generated software.
Controlled designer-developer trials show adaptive AI boundary objects improve alignment but can cause premature convergence, a transferable coordination trade-off.
The three-layer model supplies a lifecycle-wide structure for assuring agent security, compliance, and maintainability, although it is conceptual rather than empirical.
A supervisor plus specialized agents and a shared global workspace offers a concrete orchestration and synchronization pattern transferable to SDLC agents.
This controlled vocabulary-learning study is an unrelated educational application with no transferable SDLC-agent mechanism.
Generated SMT and Python checkers more than double key requirements-validation outcomes, providing a concrete hybrid formal-verification remedy.
The paper directly investigates cooperative LLM agents on a GitHub repository-documentation task, making it primary empirical MAS-for-SE evidence.
A benchmark across agent frameworks and LLM backbones exposes roughly 50 percent completion and a phase-based failure taxonomy for robust agent engineering.
This ethnochemical maize-fermentation study is unrelated to LLM agents or software engineering.
PairCoder directly compares specialized Navigator and Driver agents with direct LLM prompting and reports substantial pass-at-one gains across code benchmarks.
This discussion of a single LLM supporting agile roles and practices offers useful SDLC background but no multi-agent mechanism or controlled evidence.
The conceptual framework identifies ambiguity, consistency, and merge-conflict problems and assigns collaborative agents across software design activities.
The BotDD research agenda surfaces trust, interruption, ethics, skills, and governance constraints for autonomous coding, testing, and project-management bots.
Production-scale forecast-aware routing and resource allocation provide a transferable remedy for LLM workload cost, utilization, and latency constraints.
LLM-generated function annotations strengthen static memory-leak analysis and reduce path explosion, offering a concrete hybrid verification method.
Fuzz4All demonstrates an LLM-driven testing loop that raises coverage and finds previously unknown bugs across diverse software systems.
This systematic review identifies prompt sensitivity, robustness, security, plagiarism, and over-reliance as concrete code-generation failure mechanisms.
Structured reasoning and continual pre-training improve long-horizon stability and tool-use robustness in an adjacent agent domain with benchmark evidence.
AXNav combines an LLM with UI models and professional review to automate accessibility testing, supplying a transferable testing and oversight pattern.
DroidAgent's measured coverage gains and long- and short-term memory design provide transferable evidence for autonomous testing, but it is single-agent.
EvalPlus exposes substantial hidden failure in standard code benchmarks by generating many additional tests, directly strengthening agent-output verification.
This commit-message demo offers evaluation and human-review tooling for a narrow single-LLM task, serving only as indirect context.
This neural scaling-law theory is unrelated to LLM agents, software engineering, or a transferable production mechanism.
The empirical code-translation study tests collaborative LLMs alongside single-model, prompt, and repair strategies and reports conditional quality gains.
The proposed role-based agentic CI/CD architecture connects goals, coding, testing, deployment, feedback, and ethics, but lacks reported empirical validation.
Code-DiTing combines distilled reasoning with majority voting to improve code evaluation accuracy, explainability, robustness, and computational efficiency.
This conceptual industrial-design co-creation framework is outside software development and provides no evaluated transferable agent mechanism.
Reflexion's episodic memory and verbal feedback loop materially improve coding performance without model retraining, offering a concrete reliability remedy.
A real-world data-system architecture combines contextual knowledge, quality-assured workflows, and human alignment into an adjacent production agent pattern.
Empirical smart-contract testing reveals low precision, task-dependent performance, answer uncertainty, and context-length limits in LLM vulnerability detection.
This non-agent survey of fairness testing supplies useful governance and testing background but only indirectly informs LLM multi-agent SDLC systems.
The LangChain overview supplies relevant orchestration, state, observability, security, and scaling background without a controlled evaluation.
This digital-psychiatry framework is an unrelated clinical application without a specific transferable SDLC-agent mechanism.
CAMEL evaluates role-playing and inception prompting for autonomous agent cooperation, providing transferable communication and specialization mechanisms outside SE.
AI-oriented program grammar reduces code-task token usage while preserving performance, offering a concrete cost-control method for coding agents.
Large-scale vulnerability experiments show general ChatGPT substantially trails domain-specific models, exposing a security-relevant specialization and reliability limit.
This industrial single-LLM SQL-optimization case study provides indirect latency and engineering-effort evidence but no multi-agent or assurance mechanism.
AutoSD grounds repair in debugger observations, reports confidence, and improves human correctness judgments through explanations.
This model-representation study offers indirect evidence that specialized SE models may underperform and that evaluation protocols affect conclusions.
This economic-simulation paper is unrelated to software-development agents and offers no concrete transferable coordination or assurance mechanism.
This is conference-proceedings front matter rather than a substantive research study.
The industrial legacy-translation case exposes scarce tests as a production validation constraint while demonstrating guided prompting for functional code conversion.
This non-LLM Mars-rover autonomy report is outside software-development multi-agent research.
Divergent vulnerability reports across nine tools show why production security assurance should combine independent analyzers rather than trust one verifier.
INTERVENOR empirically evaluates specialized Code Learner and Code Teacher roles with compiler feedback against direct-model baselines on SE tasks.
This generic agile-methods review supplies indirect role and coordination background but predates and does not study LLM agents.
Equivalent-benchmark and adversarial evaluations expose reproducibility, robustness, and model-selection risks relevant to reliable coding-agent assessment.
This broad conceptual discussion of human learning with AI is unrelated to production software-development agent systems.
The controlled PEFT-versus-context comparison demonstrates a concrete way to lower recurring compute and memory costs while improving task accuracy.
Efficient code-change representation offers useful specialization and cost evidence but does not evaluate LLM agents or multi-agent workflows.
This is conference-proceedings front matter rather than a substantive paper on testing or agents.
This federated-learning monograph concerns decentralized model training rather than LLM agents or software-development automation.
This neuromorphic edge-computing application is unrelated to LLM agents or software engineering.
This is empirical-software-engineering conference front matter rather than an individual research contribution.
Compiler-testing methods for input generation, test oracles, efficient execution, and bug actionability provide transferable verification infrastructure for generated code.
